body: Scientific abstracts mix contributions with background, motivation, and meta-language, so tools that read them as-is cannot separate what a field produces from what it discusses. We present Drift Inspector, an open-source system for measuring and exploring how a research field changes over time at the level of Atomic Contribution Claims (ACCs): decontextualized, contribution-bearing propositions an LLM extracts from each abstract before analysis. The system clusters these claims across years into an interactive map where every trend traces back to the claims and papers behind it. Applied to six years of EMNLP, it shows the field shifting away from classic NLP tasks toward LLM-era capabilities such as reasoning and multimodality -- a movement that keyword or whole-abstract counts blur. The released data extend beyond EMNLP: the same pipeline has processed the full ACL Anthology (346k claims, 80k abstracts, 423 venues). Extraction is human-validated and clustering checked against an external manually constructed taxonomy.
summaryZh: Drift Inspector 是一个开源系统，旨在通过提取科研摘要中的“原子贡献声明”（Atomic Contribution Claims, ACC）来追踪科研领域的演进。该系统利用大模型将摘要转化为去语境化的贡献陈述，并进行聚类分析。通过对 EMNLP 等会议数据的分析，该工具揭示了 NLP 领域从传统任务向大模型时代推理与多模态能力的深层范式转移。该研究不仅提供了分析科研趋势的新方法，还发布了覆盖 ACL Anthology 的大规模数据集，为科学计量学研究提供了有力支持。

glossary.explanationZh: 原子贡献声明，指从科研摘要中提取的、去除了背景描述的最小化核心贡献陈述。
科学漂移，指科研领域的研究重点、方法论和关注点随时间发生的演变。
计算语言学协会的数字图书馆，收录了大量NLP领域的学术论文。
聚类分析，在此处用于将相似的科研贡献归类以识别研究趋势。
